title: Introducing WebMCP: Agents in the Browser — RL Nabors
talk_summary: The talk explains MCP transports, MCP apps, and WebMCP for exposing browser page functions as agent tools. It is mostly a browser/MCP design talk; the transferable parts are MCP resource preloading, HTTP-hosted MCP endpoints, tool visibility, and direct browser tool exposure for QA.

takeaways.technique: Preload MCP resources instead of tool-fetching docs
takeaways.what_they_do: They expose docs/rubrics as MCP resources so the harness can pre-prime context, rather than making the model call tools to fetch markdown.
takeaways.evidence_quote: resources could also allow harnesses to decide when to pre-prime that context with docs

takeaways.technique: HTTP MCP endpoint over stdio config
takeaways.what_they_do: They host MCP as a web service at a URL so clients add a connector with a name and URL instead of per-agent JSON command configs.
takeaways.evidence_quote: Give it a name, and put in a URL

takeaways.technique: Hide app-only tools from the model
takeaways.what_they_do: They mark navigation/UI-only tools with app visibility so the model does not call them and return a big JSON blob.
takeaways.evidence_quote: set visibility app there just to make sure that the model's not going to try to use that

takeaways.technique: Expose app actions as browser tools for QA
takeaways.what_they_do: They register page functions/forms as WebMCP tools so browser agents call direct functions instead of screenshotting or traversing the DOM.
takeaways.evidence_quote: Wouldn't it be great if they just had a way to call the same functions and links you already have in your JavaScript directly from the page
